verses.text: James, a servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered among the nations: Greetings.
My brothers and sisters, when all kinds of trials come your way, consider it a joy,
because you know that when your faith is tested, it develops endurance.
Let endurance finish its work so you can be mature and complete, lacking nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to everyone without criticizing, and it will be given to you.
But ask in faith without doubting, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, pushed and tossed by the wind.
That person shouldn’t expect to receive anything from the Lord.
They’re divided inside and unstable in everything they do.
Believers in humble circumstances should take pride in their high position.
But the rich should take pride in being brought low, because they’ll pass away like a wildflower.
The sun rises with scorching heat and dries up the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is gone. In the same way, the rich will fade away while going about their business.
Blessed is the person who endures testing, because after standing firm, they’ll receive the crown of life that the Lord promised to those who love him.
No one being tempted should say, “God is tempting me.” God isn’t tempted by evil, and he doesn’t tempt anyone.
Each person is tempted when they’re dragged away and trapped by their own desires.
Then desire gets pregnant and gives birth to sin; and when sin grows up, it gives birth to death.
Don’t be fooled, my dear brothers and sisters.
Every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights, who doesn’t change like shifting shadows.
He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, so we would be a kind of firstfruits of all he created.
Understand this, my dear brothers and sisters: everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to get angry,
because human anger doesn’t produce the righteousness God desires.
So get rid of all moral filth and the evil that’s so common, and humbly welcome the word planted in you, which can save you.
Don’t just listen to the word and fool yourselves. Do what it says.
Anyone who listens to the word but doesn’t do it is like someone who looks at their face in a mirror
and, after looking, walks away and immediately forgets what they look like.
But the person who looks closely into the perfect law that gives freedom and keeps at it—not forgetting what they heard, but doing it—will be blessed in what they do.
If someone thinks they’re religious but can’t control their tongue, they’re fooling themselves, and their religion is worthless.
Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: care for orphans and widows in their trouble and keep yourself from being polluted by the world.
